cur-fossil-wellington.dateNote: In 1830 the magistrate George Ranken found giant fossil bones here; Thomas Mitchell collected more the same year. Richard Owen named Diprotodon from them in 1838. The bones are Ice Age (Pleistocene), under 2 million years old.
cur-fossil-wellington.summary: Where Australia's giant extinct animals, the megafauna, were first found.

cur-fossil-cuddie-springs.dateNote: In 1876 the Yeomans family dug a well here in New South Wales and hit giant bones; William B. Clarke sent some to Richard Owen. They include Diprotodon and the giant bird Genyornis: Ice Age bones, well under 1 million years old.
cur-fossil-cuddie-springs.summary: A claypan in New South Wales full of the bones of Australia's giant Ice Age animals.

q1952802.dateNote: Jim Bowler found Mungo Lady in July 1968; he found Mungo Man nearby in February 1974.

cur-fossil-kow-swamp.dateNote: In 1968 Alan Thorne began digging this burial ground in northern Victoria, after bones turned up here in 1962. By 1972 more than 22 people had been found. They are about 0.02–0.013 million years old (Late Ice Age).
cur-fossil-kow-swamp.summary: An Ice Age burial ground in Victoria whose people had heavy, archaic-looking skulls.

cur-fossil-naracoorte.dateNote: In 1969 cavers Rod Wells and Grant Gartrell squeezed into a hidden chamber of Victoria Fossil Cave, South Australia, full of the bones of giant kangaroos, marsupial lions and wombats. They span about the last 500,000 years (0.5 million years). World Heritage since 1994.

cur-fossil-dinosaur-cove.dateNote: In 1980 Tim Flannery and John Long found dinosaur bones in the sea cliffs of Victoria; tunnels were dug in later. The rock is about 106 million years old (Early Cretaceous), when this coast lay near the South Pole: home of the big-eyed Leaellynasaura.

cur-find-cloggs-cave.dateNote: Two tiny fireplaces, each with a carved stick smeared with fat, 11,000-12,000 years old, match a GunaiKurnai ritual described in the 1800s: about 500 generations of one practice (David et al., Nature Human Behaviour, 2024).
